subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year was Khrushchev removed from power?
questions.explain: Khrushchev was ousted by his Presidium colleagues in October 1964, ending the period studied.

questions.q: What slogan summed up Bolshevik appeal in 1917?
questions.explain: 'Peace, Land and Bread' captured Bolshevik promises to a war-weary, hungry population.

questions.q: Which reactionary tutor heavily influenced Alexander III's policies?
questions.explain: Pobedonostsev, Procurator of the Holy Synod, championed autocracy, Orthodoxy and Russification under Alexander III.

questions.q: Stalin's first Five-Year Plan, launched in 1928, prioritised what?
questions.explain: The first Five-Year Plan (1928-32) emphasised heavy industry such as coal, steel and machinery.

questions.q: Which war's defeats helped spark unrest in 1905?
questions.explain: Humiliating defeats in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-05 fuelled discontent leading to revolution.

questions.q: Stolypin's agrarian reforms after 1906 aimed to create what?
options: A class of prosperous independent peasants
questions.explain: Stolypin sought to break up the commune and foster a wealthy, loyal peasant class (his 'wager on the strong').

questions.q: Which ideological doctrine did Stalin champion against Trotsky?
questions.explain: Stalin advanced 'Socialism in One Country' against Trotsky's 'Permanent Revolution'.

questions.q: Which 1918 treaty took Russia out of World War I?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (March 1918) ended Russian participation in WWI at great territorial cost.

questions.q: By what name did Russians call World War II on the Eastern Front?
questions.explain: The 1941-45 conflict with Nazi Germany is known in Russia as the Great Patriotic War.

questions.q: Which financial obligation bound former serfs to the state for decades after 1861?
questions.explain: Freed serfs had to make redemption payments, originally spread over 49 years, to compensate landowners for land allotments.

questions.q: Which minister drove Russian industrialisation and the gold standard in the 1890s?
questions.explain: Sergei Witte, as Finance Minister, expanded railways and put the rouble on the gold standard in 1897.

questions.q: Whose 1934 assassination is often seen as a pretext for the Great Terror?
questions.explain: The murder of Leningrad party boss Sergei Kirov in December 1934 was used to justify mass purges.

questions.q: Which local self-government institutions did Alexander II establish in 1864?
questions.explain: The 1864 reform created elected zemstva, rural district and provincial councils responsible for local services.

questions.q: The major show trials of Old Bolsheviks occurred chiefly in which years?
questions.explain: The Moscow show trials of 1936-38 condemned figures like Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin.

questions.q: What did the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1921 permit?
options: Limited private trade and small business
questions.explain: The NEP allowed a tax in kind and limited private trade to revive the shattered economy.

questions.q: Which 1921 uprising helped persuade Lenin to change economic course?
questions.explain: The 1921 Kronstadt mutiny by formerly loyal sailors shocked Lenin into adopting the NEP.

questions.q: What term described the forced merging of peasant farms from 1929?
questions.explain: Collectivisation forced peasants into kolkhozy, prompting resistance and famine.

questions.q: What was the harsh economic policy of the Civil War period called?
questions.explain: War Communism (1918-21) involved grain requisitioning and nationalisation to supply the Red Army.

questions.q: In what year did Stalin die, paving the way for new leadership?
questions.explain: Stalin died in March 1953, beginning a power struggle eventually won by Khrushchev.

questions.q: What did the October Manifesto of 1905 promise?
options: A constitution and an elected Duma
questions.explain: The October Manifesto granted civil liberties and an elected State Duma, helping to defuse the 1905 Revolution.

questions.q: What policy of forced cultural assimilation did Alexander III intensify?
questions.explain: Alexander III pursued Russification, imposing Russian language and Orthodoxy on minority nationalities.

questions.q: In which month and year did the monarchy fall in the February Revolution?
questions.explain: The February Revolution of 1917, in early March by the Western calendar, led to Nicholas II's abdication.

questions.q: The 1932-33 famine hit which region especially hard?
questions.explain: Ukraine suffered catastrophic famine (the Holodomor) during 1932-33 amid collectivisation.

questions.q: Alexander II became known by which epithet for his early reforms?
questions.explain: For emancipating the serfs and other reforms Alexander II was dubbed the 'Tsar Liberator'.

questions.q: At which 1956 Congress did Khrushchev denounce Stalin's crimes?
questions.explain: Khrushchev's 'Secret Speech' attacking Stalin's cult of personality was delivered at the 20th Party Congress in 1956.

questions.q: Who led the Provisional Government by mid-1917?
questions.explain: Alexander Kerensky became head of the Provisional Government in July 1917.

questions.q: Which 1942-43 battle marked the turning point on the Eastern Front?
questions.explain: The Battle of Stalingrad (1942-43) ended in a decisive Soviet victory and turned the war.

questions.q: In which month did the Bolsheviks seize power in 1917?
questions.explain: The Bolsheviks took power in the October Revolution of 1917 (early November by the Western calendar).

questions.q: In which year did Alexander II issue the Emancipation Edict freeing the serfs?
questions.explain: The Emancipation of the Serfs was decreed in February 1861, freeing roughly 23 million privately owned serfs.

questions.q: In which year did Germany invade the USSR in Operation Barbarossa?
questions.explain: Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, began on 22 June 1941.
